result.title: FOCUS: Active Critic Learning for Long-Horizon Language Model Agents
result.summary: Sparse outcome rewards make it difficult for long-horizon language-model agents to assign credit to earlier actions. Learned critics provide value estimates for intermediate states, but these estimates can be inaccurate, while estimating intermediate values with repetitive continuation samples from points within a trajectory incurs substantial costs. To mitigate these issues, we introduce FOCUS, an RL method that uses selective branching to help the critic network learn its value estimator. The rollout controller facilitates active learning for the critic by sampling continuations from states that are expected to most reduce the critic's estimation error. These refined value estimates then score the segment between consecutive states with a TD($λ$) advantage, while the sampled evidence supplies training targets for the critic. FOCUS supports long-horizon agentic reinforcement learning through a modular context-management interface that decouples context management from rollout allocation. Our experiments show that using compaction-induced segment boundaries for value estimation and credit assignment, FOCUS outperforms GRPO and VinePPO with matched per-step generation budgets on legal reasoning, deep search, and code localization benchmarks, improving held-out accuracy at Qwen3.5-9B scale by 7.2 points over the strongest baseline on BrowseComp-Plus (55.4 vs. 48.2) and by 4.1 points on DeonticBench (56.5 vs. 52.4).

AI.brief_summary: 提出 FOCUS，一种面向长时程语言模型智能体的 RL 方法：用选择性分支从最可能降低 critic 估值误差的状态处采样续写，再以 TD(λ) 优势在压缩片段间完成信用分配，在深度检索、法律推理与代码定位基准上优于 GRPO 和 VinePPO。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按估值误差主动分配续写预算、并用片段级优势打分来定位关键步骤的思路，可供核查 LVR 中的贡献分配、轨迹监督与分支/停止决策，但论文是纯文本智能体工作，未涉及视觉证据与 latent 状态生成。
